text.p: Bonds were well-supported in the short to medium end of the curve although trade was thin, while at the longer end Spain was setting the trend.
The spread between the two Iberian markets' 10-year cash bond widened slightly, largely reflecting the lack of liquidity in Portugal, traders said.
"The buyers want prices to ease further but sellers will not let go the paper because they think Spain may recover, in part at least, the recent declines," said one trader.
Traders said that the shorter end was supported by confidence that the Bank of Portugal will soon cut rates again.
But the longer end was restrained by the wide yield spread with Spain. "These spreads are only explained by the lack of liquidity," said another trader.
